The splitting lemma uses the supplier's notions of rational pure Hodge structure, Weil operator, polarization, positive definite h(x,y)=Q(Cx,ybar), type orthogonality, rational sub-Hodge structure and Tate shift, and its componentwise bidegree computations. Read from the batch-35 manifest; the consumer adds no hypothesis and weakens no claim. In-run supplier, level 2.

The analytification lemma produces a compact smooth complex manifold and a positive closed real (1,1)-form on it, so it consumes the supplier's conventions for the complex structure, the orientation and volume normalisation, complex-valued forms with bidegree splitting, positivity of (1,1)-forms and the epsilon(k) convention. The supplier's AC sentence is part of the page conventions and the consumer states AC explicitly. In-run supplier, level 2.

The consumer constructs a smooth complex manifold from standard smooth charts and holomorphic transitions, so it requires the supplier's notion of a complex manifold (maximal holomorphic atlas, induced smooth atlas, complex structure J with J^2=-1, holomorphic bundles). Read from the batch-31 manifest, the supplier states exactly these notions for complex dimension m>=1; the consumer works over C and adds compactness and second countability, which are not part of the supplier. In-run supplier, level 0; authored text owed to Step 3.

Read from the batch-35 manifest; the supplier's hypotheses (compact smooth manifold, AC) are met. In-run supplier, level 8.

The theorem is stated inside the supplier's conventions: Kaehler form omega, epsilon(k), the bidegree decomposition, positive closed real (1,1)-forms, the polarization definition for rational Hodge structures and the Tate shift used for the high-degree transport. Read from the batch-35 manifest; nothing is reinterpreted. In-run supplier, level 2.
